basic_information.title: AI-Powered Diagnostic Assistance and Medical Imaging Classification
basic_information.summary: A deep learning framework for classifying medical images (X-rays and MRIs) to assist radiologists in early anomaly detection.

abstract: Medical imaging is a crucial diagnostic tool, but the manual review process by radiologists is time-consuming and prone to human error, particularly under heavy workloads. This research presents an AI-powered diagnostic assistant that leverages Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to classify X-ray and MRI scans for abnormalities such as tumors, fractures, and pneumonia. The system provides a secondary review mechanism, highlighting regions of interest using Class Activation Mapping (CAM) to ensure interpretability. Evaluated on large public datasets, the model achieved over 92% accuracy. This tool aims to enhance diagnostic throughput and improve patient outcomes by accelerating the detection of critical conditions.
problem_statement: Radiologists often face overwhelming caseloads, leading to diagnostic delays and potential errors in identifying subtle anomalies in medical scans. A reliable, automated secondary review system is necessary to prioritize critical cases and reduce the cognitive load on medical professionals.

primary: Develop a CNN-based model for classifying abnormalities in medical images.
Create a web interface for radiologists to upload scans and receive AI-generated insights.
Implement interpretability features to explain the model's predictions.
secondary: Optimize the model for fast inference on standard clinical hardware.
Compare the performance of different neural network architectures.

included: Binary and multi-class classification of X-rays.
excluded: Direct integration with hospital PACS systems.
Final medical diagnosis without human oversight.
scope.deployment_context: Cloud-hosted web application with GPU-accelerated inference backend.

reasons: Requires deep understanding of computer vision and medical data.
Handling large datasets and complex neural architectures.

expected_outcomes: A trained classification model with high accuracy.
An interactive web dashboard for clinicians.
A comprehensive research paper documenting the methodology and results.
limitations: Model performance is highly dependent on the quality of training data.
Does not replace human medical professionals.
May struggle with rare anomalies not present in the training set.
future_scope: Integrate with electronic health record (EHR) systems.
Expand to 3D image analysis like CT scans.
Implement federated learning to preserve patient privacy.
